text: [briskly] In 1994, a railway lab in Japan set a trap like this. A hundred lights. Then, red. Twelve people just watched. Five pressed anyway. Ten lights later, three of them did it again. Twelve others got one extra rule: point at the light and say it. Not one pressed.
prev: Tap your foot on every green light. Only green. Did you tap? She did.
next: After a hundred times, your hand stops waiting for your brain. That's how the cereal ends up in the fridge. Pointing and saying it makes your hand wait. Which is why Japan's train drivers point at their signals, and shout.
